source.text: וְזֶ֨ה הַדָּבָ֜ר אֲשֶֽׁר־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם לְקַדֵּ֥שׁ אֹתָ֖ם לְכַהֵ֣ן לִ֑י לְ֠קַח פַּ֣ר אֶחָ֧ד בֶּן־בָּקָ֛ר וְאֵילִ֥ם שְׁנַ֖יִם תְּמִימִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] the thing which you will do to them to consecrate them to serve as priests to me: take one young bull, a son of [the] herd, and two rams, unblemished,

en.L: And this [is] the thing that you shall do to them to consecrate them to serve as priests to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}: take one bull, a son of the herd, and two rams without blemish,
en.B: Here is what you are to do to consecrate them as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} priests: take one young bull and two rams with no defect,
en.R: This is how you must set Aaron and his sons apart to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests. Take one young bull and two rams. The animals must have nothing wrong with them.

decisions.choice: consecrate: make holy, set apart for God
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something or someone holy, that is, to set it apart as belonging to God and fit for his service. The rites of this chapter carry out the command of 28:41.

decisions.choice: them: Aaron and his sons
decisions.reason: The chapter goes on from the garments of chapter 28, which ends with Aaron and his sons (28:41-43). Verse 4 names them.

decisions.choice: a son of the herd ... unblemished: a young bull, and animals sound and whole
decisions.reason: "Son of the herd" means a young animal from the cattle. "Unblemished" means whole, with no defect, as every animal offered to God had to be (12:5; Leviticus 22:19-22).

decisions.choice: Aaron and his sons
decisions.reason: Readable names the people meant by "them" and puts the requirement about the animals in a sentence of its own.

source.text: וְלֶ֣חֶם מַצּ֗וֹת וְחַלֹּ֤ת מַצֹּת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וּרְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּשָּׁ֑מֶן סֹ֥לֶת חִטִּ֖ים תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and bread of unleavened [loaves] and cakes of unleavened [bread] mixed with oil and wafers of unleavened [bread] smeared with oil; [of] fine flour of wheats you will make them.

en.L: and bread of unleavened [loaves], and unleavened ring-cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil; of fine flour of wheat you shall make them.
en.B: and unleavened bread, with unleavened loaves that have oil mixed in and thin unleavened wafers spread with oil. Use fine wheat flour for all of them.
en.R: Also get unleavened bread, made without yeast. Make some loaves with olive oil mixed into the dough, and some thin wafers with oil spread on top. Use the best wheat flour.

decisions.choice: cakes: ring-shaped or pierced loaves
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to pierce, and probably names a round loaf with a hole in it or one pricked through. It was a thicker loaf than the wafer.

decisions.choice: smeared: spread with oil
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for anointing (verse 7). The thin wafers had oil brushed over them, while the loaves had oil mixed into the dough.

decisions.choice: fine flour: finely ground flour, the best
decisions.reason: The word names flour ground fine, the kind used for offerings and for honored guests (Genesis 18:6; Leviticus 2:1).

decisions.choice: olive oil ... made without yeast
decisions.reason: The oil of the offerings was olive oil (27:20; verse 40), so Readable says so, and it explains "unleavened" as the style guide sets.

source.text: וְנָתַתָּ֤ אוֹתָם֙ עַל־סַ֣ל אֶחָ֔ד וְהִקְרַבְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם בַּסָּ֑ל וְאֶ֨ת־הַפָּ֔ר וְאֵ֖ת שְׁנֵ֥י הָאֵילִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put them on one basket and bring them near in the basket, and the young bull and the two rams.

en.L: And you shall put them in one basket, and you shall bring them near in the basket, and the bull and the two rams.
en.B: Place them all in a single basket and present them in it, along with the bull and the two rams.
en.R: Put all the bread in one basket. Bring the basket as an offering, together with the bull and the two rams.

decisions.choice: bring near: present before God, offer
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring something close, and it is the usual word for presenting an offering to God (Leviticus 1:2-3). The same verb is used for bringing Aaron and his sons forward in verses 4 and 8.

decisions.choice: Bring the basket as an offering
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that "bring near" means to present it as an offering.

source.text: וְאֶת־אַהֲרֹ֤ן וְאֶת־בָּנָיו֙ תַּקְרִ֔יב אֶל־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְרָחַצְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֖ם בַּמָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And Aaron and his sons you will bring near to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting and wash them with water.

en.L: And Aaron and his sons you shall bring near to the entrance of the tent of meeting, and you shall wash them with water.
en.B: Next, have Aaron and his sons come forward to the doorway of the tent of meeting, and bathe them with water.
en.R: Have Aaron and his sons come to the door of the tent of meeting. Use water to wash them.

decisions.choice: tent of meeting: the tabernacle, where God meets his people
decisions.reason: The tent is named for its purpose: there God meets with Moses and with Israel (verses 42-43; 25:22). The rites take place at its entrance, in the courtyard, where the people could gather (Leviticus 8:3-4).

decisions.choice: wash: a washing that makes them clean before they are dressed
decisions.reason: Washing with water comes first, before the holy garments are put on (Leviticus 8:6; 16:4). The priests are to wash again whenever they serve (30:19-21).

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ אֶת־הַבְּגָדִ֗ים וְהִלְבַּשְׁתָּ֤ אֶֽת־אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶת־הַכֻּתֹּ֔נֶת וְאֵת֙ מְעִ֣יל הָאֵפֹ֔ד וְאֶת־הָאֵפֹ֖ד וְאֶת־הַחֹ֑שֶׁן וְאָפַדְתָּ֣ ל֔וֹ בְּחֵ֖שֶׁב הָאֵפֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take the garments and clothe Aaron [with] the tunic and the robe of the ephod and the ephod and the breastpiece, and gird [the ephod] to him with the band of the ephod.

en.L: And you shall take the garments and clothe Aaron [with] the tunic, and the robe of the ephod, and the ephod, and the breastpiece; and you shall gird him with the band of the ephod.
en.B: Then take the priestly garments and put them on Aaron: the tunic, the robe that goes under the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece. Tie the ephod around him with its woven band.
en.R: Take the special clothes and dress Aaron in them. Put on him the tunic, the robe, the ephod and the breastpiece. Tie the ephod in place with its belt.

decisions.choice: the garments: the holy garments made for Aaron in chapter 28
decisions.reason: The garments are the ones God described in chapter 28 (28:2-4), made "for glory and for beauty". They are put on him here in the order of dressing, from the inner tunic outward.

decisions.choice: gird with the band: fasten the ephod with its woven waistband
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word "ephod" itself and means to tie the ephod on. The band was woven of the same materials as the ephod and fastened it at the waist (28:8).

decisions.choice: priestly garments / special clothes; the robe that goes under the ephod
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of garments these are. Balanced explains "robe of the ephod" as the robe worn under it (28:31); Readable shortens it to "the robe" and calls the band a belt.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ הַמִּצְנֶ֖פֶת עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וְנָתַתָּ֛ אֶת־נֵ֥זֶר הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ עַל־הַמִּצְנָֽפֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put the turban on his head and put the crown of holiness on the turban.

en.L: And you shall set the turban on his head, and you shall put the crown of holiness on the turban.
en.B: Place the turban on his head and fasten the holy crown to the turban.
en.R: Put the turban on his head. Then attach the holy crown, the gold plate, to the turban.

decisions.choice: the crown of holiness: the gold plate on the front of the turban
decisions.reason: The word means a crown or a sign of dedication. Here it is the plate of pure gold engraved "Holy to Yahweh" that was tied to the front of the turban (28:36-37); 39:30 calls it "the plate of the holy crown".

decisions.choice: the gold plate
decisions.reason: Readable says what the holy crown was, from 28:36 and 39:30.

source.text: וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת־שֶׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָ֔ה וְיָצַקְתָּ֖ עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וּמָשַׁחְתָּ֖ אֹתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take the oil of the anointing and pour [it] on his head and anoint him.

en.L: And you shall take the oil of anointing and pour [it] on his head and anoint him.
en.B: Then take the anointing oil and pour it over his head. In this way you will anoint him.
en.R: Then take the anointing oil and pour some on his head to anoint him.

decisions.choice: anoint: mark him as set apart for God's service
decisions.reason: Pouring the holy oil on Aaron's head marks him as consecrated to God (30:30; Leviticus 8:12; Psalm 133:2). In Israel kings and priests were anointed for their office.

decisions.choice: the anointing oil: the holy oil made by God's own recipe
decisions.reason: The oil is olive oil blended with spices, made as 30:22-33 describes and used for nothing else.

source.text: וְאֶת־בָּנָ֖יו תַּקְרִ֑יב וְהִלְבַּשְׁתָּ֖ם כֻּתֳּנֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And his sons you will bring near and clothe them [with] tunics,

en.L: And his sons you shall bring near and clothe them [with] tunics,
en.B: Then bring his sons forward and dress them in tunics,
en.R: Next bring Aaron's sons and put tunics on them.

decisions.choice: tunics: the plainer garments of the ordinary priests
decisions.reason: Aaron's sons wear tunics, sashes and caps (28:40), not the ephod, breastpiece and robe that belong to Aaron alone as the chief priest.

decisions.choice: Aaron's sons
decisions.reason: Readable names Aaron for "his" and ends the sentence here; Literal and Balanced run on into verse 9.

source.text: וְחָגַרְתָּ֩ אֹתָ֨ם אַבְנֵ֜ט אַהֲרֹ֣ן וּבָנָ֗יו וְחָבַשְׁתָּ֤ לָהֶם֙ מִגְבָּעֹ֔ת וְהָיְתָ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם כְּהֻנָּ֖ה לְחֻקַּ֣ת עוֹלָ֑ם וּמִלֵּאתָ֥ יַֽד־אַהֲרֹ֖ן וְיַד־בָּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: and you will gird them [with] a sash, Aaron and his sons, and bind on them caps, and will be to them [the] priesthood as a statute of perpetuity. And you will fill [the] hand of Aaron and [the] hand of his sons.

en.L: and you shall gird them [with] a sash, Aaron and his sons, and you shall bind caps on them; and the priesthood shall belong to them as a statute forever. And you shall fill the hand of Aaron and the hand of his sons.
en.B: and tie sashes around them, both Aaron and his sons, and fit caps on their heads. The priesthood will belong to them by a statute for all time. And you will ordain Aaron and his sons.
en.R: Tie sashes around the waists of Aaron and his sons, and put caps on the sons' heads. The priesthood will belong to them and their descendants for all time. This is a rule that will not change. In this way you will ordain Aaron and his sons as priests.

decisions.choice: fill the hand: ordain, install in the priest's office
decisions.reason: "Fill the hand" is the Hebrew way of saying that someone is installed in an office, especially as priest (28:41; Judges 17:5, 12; 1 Kings 13:33). Where the idiom comes from is not certain: it may come from placing the offerings in the priests' hands (verse 24), or from giving them their authority or their share. The ram of verse 22 is named for it, "the ram of filling", and the whole seven-day rite is the filling of their hands (verse 35).

decisions.choice: a statute forever: a fixed rule for all time
decisions.reason: "Statute" is a fixed rule; "forever" means for all generations to come. The priesthood belongs to Aaron's family for as long as Israel continues (40:15; Numbers 25:13).

decisions.choice: bind caps on them: on Aaron's sons
decisions.reason: "Them" most likely means the sons, who wear caps (28:40), while Aaron wears the turban (verse 6). It may also include Aaron with the sons, as the sash does.

decisions.choice: ordain
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the idiom "fill the hand". Balanced and Readable say what it means, "ordain".

decisions.choice: and their descendants ... This is a rule that will not change
decisions.reason: Readable says that "forever" includes the generations after them, and explains "statute" in a sentence of its own.

source.text: וְהִקְרַבְתָּ֙ אֶת־הַפָּ֔ר לִפְנֵ֖י אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֑ד וְסָמַ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הַפָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will bring near the young bull before the tent of meeting, and will lay Aaron and his sons their hands on [the] head of the bull.

en.L: And you shall bring the bull near before the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.
en.B: Lead the bull to the front of the tent of meeting, where Aaron and his sons are to place their hands on its head.
en.R: Bring the bull to the front of the tent of meeting. Aaron and his sons must put their hands on the bull's head.

decisions.choice: lay their hands on: press their hands on the animal's head
decisions.reason: The verb means to lean or press. By pressing their hands on the head, the offerers mark the animal as their own offering, given in their place (Leviticus 1:4; 4:4; 16:21). Here Aaron and his sons are the offerers, so the offering is for them.

source.text: וְשָׁחַטְתָּ֥ אֶת־הַפָּ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will slaughter the young bull before Yahweh, [at the] entrance of the tent of meeting.

en.L: And you shall slaughter the bull before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [at] the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: Slaughter the bull there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, at the doorway of the tent of meeting.
en.R: Then kill the bull there at the door of the tent of meeting, in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: before Yahweh: in his presence, at his dwelling
decisions.reason: The tent is God's dwelling (25:8), so what is done at its entrance is done in his presence.

decisions.choice: you will slaughter: Moses acts as priest at the ordination
decisions.reason: Until Aaron and his sons are ordained, Moses carries out the priestly acts himself, as Leviticus 8:14-30 tells.

source.text: וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ מִדַּ֣ם הַפָּ֔ר וְנָתַתָּ֛ה עַל־קַרְנֹ֥ת הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ בְּאֶצְבָּעֶ֑ךָ וְאֶת־כָּל־הַדָּ֣ם תִּשְׁפֹּ֔ךְ אֶל־יְס֖וֹד הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take some of [the] blood of the bull and put [it] on [the] horns of the altar with your finger, and all the blood you will pour out at [the] base of the altar.

en.L: And you shall take some of the blood of the bull and put [it] on the horns of the altar with your finger, and all the blood you shall pour out at the base of the altar.
en.B: With your finger, smear some of the bull's blood on the horns of the altar, and pour out all the rest beside the altar's base.
en.R: Use your finger to put some of the bull's blood on the corners of the altar that stick up like horns. Then pour out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar.

decisions.choice: the horns of the altar: the raised corners of the bronze altar
decisions.reason: The altar of burnt offering had a horn at each of its four corners, made in one piece with it (27:1-2). Blood on the horns marks the altar as cleansed (verse 36; Leviticus 4:7; 8:15).

decisions.choice: all the blood: all the blood that is left
decisions.reason: Some of the blood has already been put on the horns; "all the blood" is the rest of it.

decisions.choice: corners ... that stick up like horns
decisions.reason: Readable explains what the horns of the altar were.

source.text: וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֗ אֶֽת־כָּל־הַחֵלֶב֮ הַֽמְכַסֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַקֶּרֶב֒ וְאֵ֗ת הַיֹּתֶ֨רֶת֙ עַל־הַכָּבֵ֔ד וְאֵת֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י הַכְּלָיֹ֔ת וְאֶת־הַחֵ֖לֶב אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲלֵיהֶ֑ן וְהִקְטַרְתָּ֖ הַמִּזְבֵּֽחָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take all the fat [which] covers the entrails and the lobe on the liver and the two kidneys and the fat which [is] on them and make [them] smoke on the altar.

en.L: And you shall take all the fat that covers the entrails, and the lobe on the liver, and the two kidneys, and the fat that [is] on them, and make [them] smoke on the altar.
en.B: Remove all the fat that covers the inner parts, the lobe that sits on the liver, and the two kidneys together with their fat, and turn them into smoke on the altar.
en.R: Cut out all the fat around the bull's insides, the piece that covers the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat. Burn them on the altar.

decisions.choice: the fat: the choicest parts, which belong to God
decisions.reason: The fat around the inner organs was counted the best part of the animal, and it always went to God on the altar (Leviticus 3:3-5, 16-17).

decisions.choice: the lobe on the liver: a piece of the liver, or the fatty covering over it
decisions.reason: The word means what is left over or what projects. It names a part of or over the liver, perhaps its long lobe or the fatty membrane that covers it. Which part is meant is not certain.

decisions.choice: make smoke: burn so that it goes up as smoke
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for burning incense and offerings. It pictures the offering rising to God as smoke (verse 18).

source.text: וְאֶת־בְּשַׂ֤ר הַפָּר֙ וְאֶת־עֹר֣וֹ וְאֶת־פִּרְשׁ֔וֹ תִּשְׂרֹ֣ף בָּאֵ֔שׁ מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה חַטָּ֖את הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And the flesh of the bull and its hide and its dung you will burn with fire outside of the camp; a sin offering it [is].

en.L: And the flesh of the bull and its hide and its dung you shall burn with fire outside the camp; it [is] a sin offering.
en.B: As for the bull's meat, its hide and its dung, burn them in a fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
en.R: But burn the rest of the bull, its meat, its skin and its dung, outside the camp. It is a sin offering, an offering to take away sin.

decisions.choice: sin offering: an offering that cleanses from sin
decisions.reason: The noun is the ordinary word for sin, used for the offering that deals with it. Its blood cleanses the altar and the people from the defilement of sin (verse 36; Leviticus 4; 16:16). For that reason it is also understood as a "purification offering".

decisions.choice: outside the camp: the meat is not eaten
decisions.reason: When a sin offering is made for the priests themselves, its meat is not eaten by them but burned outside the camp (Leviticus 4:11-12; 8:17). Hebrews 13:11-12 recalls this rule.

decisions.choice: an offering to take away sin
decisions.reason: Readable keeps "sin offering" and adds a short explanation of its purpose.

source.text: וְאֶת־הָאַ֥יִל הָאֶחָ֖ד תִּקָּ֑ח וְסָ֨מְכ֜וּ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָאָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And the ram, the one, you will take, and will lay Aaron and his sons their hands on [the] head of the ram.

en.L: And the one ram you shall take, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
en.B: Next take the first ram. Aaron and his sons are to rest their hands on the ram's head.
en.R: Then take one of the rams. Aaron and his sons must put their hands on its head.

decisions.choice: the one ram: the first of the two rams
decisions.reason: Verse 1 called for two rams. This is the first; verse 19 turns to "the second ram".

decisions.choice: lay their hands: as with the bull
decisions.reason: The rite is the same as in verse 10: the priests mark the ram as their own offering.

source.text: וְשָׁחַטְתָּ֖ אֶת־הָאָ֑יִל וְלָֽקַחְתָּ֙ אֶת־דָּמ֔וֹ וְזָרַקְתָּ֥ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will slaughter the ram and take its blood and splash [it] on the altar all around.

en.L: And you shall slaughter the ram, and you shall take its blood and dash [it] against the altar all around.
en.B: Kill the ram, collect its blood, and throw it against the altar on all sides.
en.R: Kill the ram. Take its blood and splash it all around the altar.

decisions.choice: splash: throw or dash the blood in quantity
decisions.reason: The verb means to toss or throw, as from a bowl, not to sprinkle drops (Leviticus 1:5, 11). A different verb, "spatter", is used in verse 21.

source.text: וְאֶ֨ת־הָאַ֔יִל תְּנַתֵּ֖חַ לִנְתָחָ֑יו וְרָחַצְתָּ֤ קִרְבּוֹ֙ וּכְרָעָ֔יו וְנָתַתָּ֥ עַל־נְתָחָ֖יו וְעַל־רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And the ram you will cut into its pieces and wash its entrails and its legs and put [them] with its pieces and with its head.

en.L: And the ram you shall cut into its pieces, and you shall wash its entrails and its legs, and put [them] with its pieces and with its head.
en.B: Divide the ram into its pieces. Wash its insides and its legs, and set them beside its pieces and its head.
en.R: Cut up the ram. Wash the inside parts and the legs, then put them together with the head and all the other pieces.

decisions.choice: wash its entrails and legs: clean the parts that would be soiled
decisions.reason: The inner parts and the legs were washed of dung and dirt before they were laid on the altar (Leviticus 1:9).

decisions.choice: with its pieces: on top of or beside them
decisions.reason: The preposition can mean "on" or "along with". Either way the washed parts are laid with the rest of the ram, so that the whole animal is burned (verse 18).

source.text: וְהִקְטַרְתָּ֤ אֶת־כָּל־הָאַ֨יִל֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עֹלָ֥ה ה֖וּא לַֽיהוָ֑ה רֵ֣יחַ נִיח֔וֹחַ אִשֶּׁ֥ה לַיהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will make smoke all the ram on the altar; a burnt offering it [is] to Yahweh, an aroma of soothing, an offering by fire to Yahweh it [is].

en.L: And you shall make the whole ram smoke on the altar. It [is] a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, an aroma of soothing; it [is] an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Send up the whole ram in smoke from the altar as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, with an aroma that pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is an offering burned with fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and its smell pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: burnt offering: an offering burned whole on the altar
decisions.reason: The word means "what goes up". Nothing of the animal is eaten; all of it goes up to God in smoke (Leviticus 1).

decisions.choice: an aroma of soothing: a pleasing aroma, an offering God accepts
decisions.reason: The phrase first appears in Genesis 8:21, after the flood. It says that God receives the offering with favor; it does not mean that God needs food.

decisions.choice: offering by fire: an offering given to God on the altar fire
decisions.reason: The word is usually linked with the word for fire, since these offerings are burned. It may instead mean a gift, since it is also used of parts that are not burned (Leviticus 24:7, 9).

decisions.choice: with an aroma that pleases him / its smell pleases him
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "an aroma of soothing". Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: וְלָ֣קַחְתָּ֔ אֵ֖ת הָאַ֣יִל הַשֵּׁנִ֑י וְסָמַ֨ךְ אַהֲרֹ֧ן וּבָנָ֛יו אֶת־יְדֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־רֹ֥אשׁ הָאָֽיִל׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take the ram, the second, and will lay Aaron and his sons their hands on [the] head of the ram.

en.L: And you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.
en.B: Then take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons are to rest their hands on its head.
en.R: Then take the second ram. Aaron and his sons must put their hands on its head.

decisions.choice: the second ram: the ram of ordination
decisions.reason: Verse 22 names this ram "the ram of ordination". Its blood and its parts are used in the rites that install the priests (verses 20-28).

source.text: וְשָׁחַטְתָּ֣ אֶת־הָאַ֗יִל וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ מִדָּמוֹ֙ וְנָֽתַתָּ֡ה עַל־תְּנוּךְ֩ אֹ֨זֶן אַהֲרֹ֜ן וְעַל־תְּנ֨וּךְ אֹ֤זֶן בָּנָיו֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית וְעַל־בֹּ֤הֶן יָדָם֙ הַיְמָנִ֔ית וְעַל־בֹּ֥הֶן רַגְלָ֖ם הַיְמָנִ֑ית וְזָרַקְתָּ֧ אֶת־הַדָּ֛ם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will slaughter the ram and take some of its blood and put [it] on [the] lobe of [the] ear of Aaron and on [the] lobe of [the] ear of his sons, the right, and on [the] thumb of their hand, the right, and on [the] big toe of their foot, the right, and splash the blood on the altar all around.

en.L: And you shall slaughter the ram, and take some of its blood and put [it] on the lobe of Aaron's [right] ear and on the lobe of his sons' right ear, and on the thumb of their right hand, and on the big toe of their right foot; and you shall dash the blood against the altar all around.
en.B: Kill this ram and take some of its blood. Put the blood on Aaron's right earlobe and on the right earlobes of his sons, on the thumbs of their right hands and the big toes of their right feet. Throw the rest of the blood against the altar all around.
en.R: Kill the ram and take some of its blood. Put some on the bottom of the right ear of Aaron and of each of his sons. Put some on the thumb of their right hands and on the big toe of their right feet. Then splash the rest of the blood all around the altar.

decisions.choice: ear, thumb and big toe: the whole person marked for God's service
decisions.reason: The text does not explain the sign. The same three places are marked when a person healed of a skin disease is cleansed (Leviticus 14:14, 17). Touching the ear, the hand and the foot, from the head to the feet, may mark the whole person as consecrated: what he hears, what he does, and where he goes.

decisions.choice: put on: carried out in Leviticus 8:23-24
decisions.reason: Leviticus 8 tells how Moses did all that this chapter commands, including this rite.

decisions.choice: the rest of the blood
decisions.reason: Some of the blood has been used on the priests; what is thrown against the altar is the rest of it.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֞ מִן־הַדָּ֨ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַֽל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ֮ וּמִשֶּׁ֣מֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה֒ וְהִזֵּיתָ֤ עַֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְעַל־בְּגָדָ֔יו וְעַל־בָּנָ֛יו וְעַל־בִּגְדֵ֥י בָנָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ וְקָדַ֥שׁ הוּא֙ וּבְגָדָ֔יו וּבָנָ֛יו וּבִגְדֵ֥י בָנָ֖יו אִתּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take some of the blood which [is] on the altar and some of the oil of the anointing and spatter [it] on Aaron and on his garments and on his sons and on the garments of his sons with him; and he will be holy, and his garments, and his sons and the garments of his sons with him.

en.L: And you shall take some of the blood that [is] on the altar and some of the anointing oil and spatter [it] on Aaron and on his garments, and on his sons and on the garments of his sons with him; and he shall be holy, and his garments, and his sons, and the garments of his sons with him.
en.B: Then take a little of the blood on the altar and of the anointing oil, and spatter it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments as well. In this way Aaron, his sons, and the garments they all wear will become holy.
en.R: Take a little of the blood from the altar and a little of the anointing oil. Sprinkle them on Aaron and his clothes, and on his sons and their clothes. This will make Aaron and his sons and their clothes holy.

decisions.choice: spatter: sprinkle in drops
decisions.reason: This verb is used for sprinkling small amounts, often with the finger (Leviticus 4:6; 8:30), unlike the verb "splash" in verse 20.

decisions.choice: he will be holy: he and his garments belong to God
decisions.reason: Blood from the altar and holy oil together set the priests and their garments apart for God's service. Leviticus 8:30 tells how it was done.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ מִן־הָ֠אַיִל הַחֵ֨לֶב וְהָֽאַלְיָ֜ה וְאֶת־הַחֵ֣לֶב׀הַֽמְכַסֶּ֣ה אֶת־הַקֶּ֗רֶב וְאֵ֨ת יֹתֶ֤רֶת הַכָּבֵד֙ וְאֵ֣ת׀שְׁתֵּ֣י הַכְּלָיֹ֗ת וְאֶת־הַחֵ֨לֶב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲלֵהֶ֔ן וְאֵ֖ת שׁ֣וֹק הַיָּמִ֑ין כִּ֛י אֵ֥יל מִלֻּאִ֖ים הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take from the ram the fat and the fat tail and the fat [which] covers the entrails and the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys and the fat which [is] on them and the thigh of the right, for a ram of ordination it [is],

en.L: And you shall take from the ram the fat and the fat tail, and the fat that covers the entrails, and the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that [is] on them, and the right thigh, for it [is] a ram of ordination,
en.B: Take the fat of this ram, its fat tail, the fat that covers the inner parts, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat around them, and the right thigh, because this ram is the ram of ordination,
en.R: Take the fat from this ram: the fat tail, the fat around its insides, the piece that covers the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat. Also take the right thigh. This ram is for the ordination of the priests.

decisions.choice: the fat tail: the broad, fatty tail of a sheep
decisions.reason: The sheep of the region had broad tails that stored fat, a choice part given to God on the altar (Leviticus 3:9).

decisions.choice: ordination: the filling, the installing of the priests
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "fill" in "fill the hand" (verse 9). This ram is the offering by which the priests are installed (Leviticus 8:22).

decisions.choice: the right thigh: the upper part of the right hind leg
decisions.reason: In later fellowship offerings the right thigh is the priest's share (Leviticus 7:32-34). At the ordination it is burned on the altar (verse 25), "for it is a ram of ordination".

source.text: וְכִכַּ֨ר לֶ֜חֶם אַחַ֗ת וַֽחַלַּ֨ת לֶ֥חֶם שֶׁ֛מֶן אַחַ֖ת וְרָקִ֣יק אֶחָ֑ד מִסַּל֙ הַמַּצּ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: and one round loaf of bread and one cake of bread of oil and one wafer from [the] basket of the unleavened [bread] which [is] before Yahweh.

en.L: and one round loaf of bread, and one cake of oil bread, and one wafer, from the basket of the unleavened [bread] that [is] before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: along with one round loaf of bread, one loaf made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that stands before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: From the basket of unleavened bread that is in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, take one loaf of plain bread, one loaf made with oil, and one thin wafer.

decisions.choice: the basket: the basket of verses 2-3
decisions.reason: One of each of the three kinds of bread described in verse 2 is taken from the basket.

decisions.choice: round loaf: a flat, round loaf of bread
decisions.reason: The word means something round, and is used of a round loaf, of a round weight (a talent), and of the plain of the Jordan.

source.text: וְשַׂמְתָּ֣ הַכֹּ֔ל עַ֚ל כַּפֵּ֣י אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְעַ֖ל כַּפֵּ֣י בָנָ֑יו וְהֵנַפְתָּ֥ אֹתָ֛ם תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will put the whole on [the] palms of Aaron and on [the] palms of his sons and wave them [as] a wave offering before Yahweh.

en.L: And you shall put all [of it] on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons, and you shall wave them [as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Set all of it on the open hands of Aaron and his sons, and present it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with a waving motion as a wave offering.
en.R: Put all these things into the hands of Aaron and his sons. Then wave them before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering, a gift lifted up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: wave: present to God with a motion of the hands
decisions.reason: The verb means to move something to and fro or to lift it up. The motion, perhaps toward the altar and back, showed that the gift was given to God. The exact movement is not known.

decisions.choice: you will wave them: Moses, while the gifts rest on the priests' hands
decisions.reason: Moses places the gifts on the priests' palms and he himself waves them (Leviticus 8:27). The priests' hands are filled, as the idiom "fill the hand" says (verse 9).

decisions.choice: a gift lifted up to him
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a wave offering is.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֤ אֹתָם֙ מִיָּדָ֔ם וְהִקְטַרְתָּ֥ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חָה עַל־הָעֹלָ֑ה לְרֵ֤יחַ נִיח֨וֹחַ֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אִשֶּׁ֥ה ה֖וּא לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take them from their hand and make [them] smoke on the altar on the burnt offering, for an aroma of soothing before Yahweh; an offering by fire it [is] to Yahweh.

en.L: And you shall take them from their hand and make [them] smoke on the altar on the burnt offering, for an aroma of soothing before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; it [is] an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Afterward take these from their hands and send them up in smoke on the altar, on top of the burnt offering, as an aroma pleasing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. This is an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then take these things from their hands and burn them on the altar, on top of the burnt offering. Their smell will please {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. It is an offering burned with fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: on the burnt offering: on top of the ram already burning
decisions.reason: The first ram was burned whole as the burnt offering (verse 18). The fat, the thigh and the bread of the second ram are laid on top of it.

decisions.choice: an aroma of soothing: an offering God accepts
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

source.text: וְלָקַחְתָּ֣ אֶת־הֶֽחָזֶ֗ה מֵאֵ֤יל הַמִּלֻּאִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאַהֲרֹ֔ן וְהֵנַפְתָּ֥ אֹת֛וֹ תְּנוּפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֥ה לְךָ֖ לְמָנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will take the breast from [the] ram of the ordination which [is] for Aaron and wave it [as] a wave offering before Yahweh, and it will be to you as a portion.

en.L: And you shall take the breast from the ram of ordination that [is] for Aaron, and wave it [as] a wave offering before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and it shall be your portion.
en.B: Then take the breast from the ram used to ordain Aaron, and present it to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering. That piece is to be your share.
en.R: Take the breast of the ram used to make Aaron a priest, and wave it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a wave offering. This part will be yours.

decisions.choice: which is for Aaron: the ram for Aaron's ordination
decisions.reason: The ram is offered for Aaron and his sons, to ordain them.

decisions.choice: your portion: Moses' share, as the one who serves as priest
decisions.reason: Moses carries out the priest's duties at the ordination, so he receives the priest's share, the breast (Leviticus 8:29). Later the breast goes to Aaron and his sons (verses 27-28; Leviticus 7:31).

source.text: וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֞ אֵ֣ת׀חֲזֵ֣ה הַתְּנוּפָ֗ה וְאֵת֙ שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הוּנַ֖ף וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר הוּרָ֑ם מֵאֵיל֙ הַמִּלֻּאִ֔ים מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאַהֲרֹ֖ן וּמֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר לְבָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, which was waved and which was raised, from [the] ram of the ordination, from [that] which [is] for Aaron and from [that] which [is] for his sons.

en.L: And you shall consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the heave offering, which was waved and which was raised up, from the ram of ordination, from what [is] Aaron's and from what [is] his sons'.
en.B: Consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, the parts of the ram of ordination that were waved and lifted up, the share that belongs to Aaron and his sons.
en.R: Set apart as holy the breast and the thigh of the ram used for ordination. These are the parts that are waved and lifted up to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they belong to Aaron and his sons.

decisions.choice: contribution: a part lifted off and set aside for God
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "raise" or "lift off" used later in this verse. It names a portion taken from a larger whole and given to God, which God then gives to the priests. It was formerly rendered "heave offering".

decisions.choice: consecrate ... which was waved and raised: a rule for the future
decisions.reason: At the ordination the thigh was burned (verses 22, 25), so verses 27-28 look ahead. From now on, the breast and the thigh of such offerings are holy and belong to the priests (Leviticus 7:31-34; 10:14-15).

decisions.choice: lifted up to the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the parts are waved and lifted, as in verses 24 and 26.

source.text: וְהָיָה֩ לְאַהֲרֹ֨ן וּלְבָנָ֜יו לְחָק־עוֹלָ֗ם מֵאֵת֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כִּ֥י תְרוּמָ֖ה ה֑וּא וּתְרוּמָ֞ה יִהְיֶ֨ה מֵאֵ֤ת בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִזִּבְחֵ֣י שַׁלְמֵיהֶ֔ם תְּרוּמָתָ֖ם לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it will be for Aaron and for his sons as a due of perpetuity from with [the] sons of Israel, for a contribution it [is]; and a contribution it will be from with [the] sons of Israel from [the] sacrifices of their peace offerings, their contribution to Yahweh.

en.L: And it shall be for Aaron and for his sons as a due forever from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, for it [is] a heave offering; and a heave offering it shall be from the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, from their sacrifices of peace offerings, their heave offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: This will be the lasting share that Aaron and his sons receive from the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}. It is a contribution: whenever the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} sacrifice fellowship offerings, this part is their contribution to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: From now on, whenever the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} offer fellowship offerings, the breast and the thigh will always belong to Aaron and his sons. These parts are the people's gift to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: a due forever: a fixed share for all time
decisions.reason: The word is the one translated "statute" in verse 9. Here it means a fixed share that is owed, the priests' lasting portion (Leviticus 10:13-15).

decisions.choice: peace offerings: offerings shared in a meal
decisions.reason: The word is related to the word for peace and wholeness. In these offerings part was burned to God, part went to the priests, and the worshipers ate the rest in a meal before God (Leviticus 3; 7:11-36).

decisions.choice: fellowship offerings
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "fellowship offerings", which names the shared meal; Literal keeps "peace offerings".

decisions.choice: the breast and the thigh ... the people's gift
decisions.reason: Readable names the two parts meant by "it" (verse 27) and says "gift" for "contribution".

source.text: וּבִגְדֵ֤י הַקֹּ֨דֶשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאַהֲרֹ֔ן יִהְי֥וּ לְבָנָ֖יו אַחֲרָ֑יו לְמָשְׁחָ֣ה בָהֶ֔ם וּלְמַלֵּא־בָ֖ם אֶת־יָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] garments of holiness which [are] for Aaron will be for his sons after him, for anointing in them and to fill in them their hand.

en.L: And the garments of holiness that [are] Aaron's shall be for his sons after him, to be anointed in them and to fill their hand in them.
en.B: The holy garments made for Aaron are to go to his sons after him. They will wear them when they are anointed and ordained.
en.R: After Aaron, his holy clothes will be passed down to his sons. They will wear these clothes when they are anointed and made priests.

decisions.choice: his sons after him: those who succeed him as chief priest
decisions.reason: The garments pass to the son who takes Aaron's place (verse 30), as they did to Eleazar (Numbers 20:26-28).

decisions.choice: to fill their hand: to ordain them
decisions.reason: See verse 9.

source.text: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים יִלְבָּשָׁ֧ם הַכֹּהֵ֛ן תַּחְתָּ֖יו מִבָּנָ֑יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָבֹ֛א אֶל־אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד לְשָׁרֵ֥ת בַּקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: Seven days will wear them the priest in his place from his sons, who will come into [the] tent of meeting to serve in the holy [place].

en.L: Seven days the priest in his place from among his sons, who comes into the tent of meeting to minister in the holy [place], shall wear them.
en.B: For seven days they are to be worn by whichever of his sons becomes priest in his place, when he enters the tent of meeting to serve in the holy place.
en.R: When one of Aaron's sons becomes chief priest in Aaron's place, he must wear these clothes for seven days. He is the one who will go into the tent of meeting to serve in the holy place.

decisions.choice: seven days: the days of his ordination
decisions.reason: Like Aaron, each successor is ordained over seven days (verse 35), wearing the holy garments throughout.

decisions.choice: the holy place: the holy part of the tent
decisions.reason: The word "holiness" here names the holy place, the outer room of the tabernacle where the lampstand, table and altar of incense stood (26:33; 28:43).

decisions.choice: chief priest
decisions.reason: The son who takes Aaron's place inherits his office as chief priest, so Readable says so.

source.text: וְאֵ֛ת אֵ֥יל הַמִּלֻּאִ֖ים תִּקָּ֑ח וּבִשַּׁלְתָּ֥ אֶת־בְּשָׂר֖וֹ בְּמָקֹ֥ם קָדֹֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] ram of the ordination you will take and boil its flesh in a place holy.

en.L: And the ram of ordination you shall take, and you shall boil its flesh in a holy place.
en.B: As for the ram of ordination, boil its meat in a holy place.
en.R: Boil the meat of the ram used for ordination. Do it in a holy place.

decisions.choice: a holy place: within the court, at the entrance of the tent
decisions.reason: Verse 32 says the meat is eaten at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and Leviticus 8:31 says it was boiled there.

source.text: וְאָכַ֨ל אַהֲרֹ֤ן וּבָנָיו֙ אֶת־בְּשַׂ֣ר הָאַ֔יִל וְאֶת־הַלֶּ֖חֶם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּסָּ֑ל פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And will eat Aaron and his sons the flesh of the ram and the bread which [is] in the basket, [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that [is] in the basket, [at] the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: Aaron and his sons are to eat the ram's meat, with the bread remaining in the basket, there at the doorway of the tent of meeting.
en.R: Then Aaron and his sons must eat the meat of the ram and the bread that is left in the basket. They must eat it at the door of the tent of meeting.

decisions.choice: they will eat: a meal in God's presence
decisions.reason: The priests eat their share of the ordination offering at God's dwelling. The meal completes their installation (verse 33).

source.text: וְאָכְל֤וּ אֹתָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כֻּפַּ֣ר בָּהֶ֔ם לְמַלֵּ֥א אֶת־יָדָ֖ם לְקַדֵּ֣שׁ אֹתָ֑ם וְזָ֥ר לֹא־יֹאכַ֖ל כִּי־קֹ֥דֶשׁ הֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they will eat them, which atonement was made by them to fill their hand to consecrate them; and a stranger not will eat, for holy they [are].

en.L: And they shall eat those things by which atonement was made, to fill their hand, to consecrate them; but a stranger shall not eat [them], for they [are] holy.
en.B: The things that were used to make atonement for them, when they were ordained and made holy, are food for them to eat. An outsider must not eat any of it, since it is holy.
en.R: These offerings made atonement for them on the day they were ordained and set apart as holy. So they must eat them. But no one who is not a priest may eat this food, because it is holy.

decisions.choice: atonement was made: their sin was dealt with and they were made fit to serve
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for making atonement: removing sin and its defilement so that the relationship with God is made right. The offerings of the ordination did this for the priests.

decisions.choice: a stranger: anyone who is not a priest
decisions.reason: The word means an outsider. Here it means anyone outside the priestly family, even an Israelite (Leviticus 22:10; Numbers 3:10).

decisions.choice: no one who is not a priest
decisions.reason: Readable says who the "stranger" is.

source.text: וְֽאִם־יִוָּתֵ֞ר מִבְּשַׂ֧ר הַמִּלֻּאִ֛ים וּמִן־הַלֶּ֖חֶם עַד־הַבֹּ֑קֶר וְשָׂרַפְתָּ֤ אֶת־הַנּוֹתָר֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ לֹ֥א יֵאָכֵ֖ל כִּי־קֹ֥דֶשׁ הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And if will be left over some of [the] flesh of the ordination or some of the bread until the morning, and you will burn the remainder with fire; not it will be eaten, for holy it [is].

en.L: And if any of the flesh of the ordination or of the bread is left over until the morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it [is] holy.
en.B: Should any of the ordination meat or the bread remain until morning, you must burn whatever is left. No one may eat it; it is holy.
en.R: Do not keep any of the meat or bread until the next morning. If some is left, burn it in a fire. It is holy, and no one may eat it.

decisions.choice: until the morning: holy food is not kept over
decisions.reason: As with the Passover lamb (12:10) and the thank offering (Leviticus 7:15), the holy meat must be eaten the same day, and what is left is burned.

decisions.choice: Do not keep ... If some is left, burn it
decisions.reason: Readable turns the condition into a plain command followed by what to do if any is left.

source.text: וְעָשִׂ֜יתָ לְאַהֲרֹ֤ן וּלְבָנָיו֙ כָּ֔כָה כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־צִוִּ֖יתִי אֹתָ֑כָה שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים תְּמַלֵּ֥א יָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will do to Aaron and to his sons thus, according to all that I have commanded you; seven days you will fill their hand.

en.L: And you shall do thus to Aaron and to his sons, according to all that I have commanded you; seven days you shall fill their hand.
en.B: Carry out for Aaron and his sons everything exactly as I have commanded you. Spend seven days ordaining them.
en.R: Do everything I have told you to do for Aaron and his sons. The ordination must last seven days.

decisions.choice: seven days: the rites are repeated over a full week
decisions.reason: The priests stay at the entrance of the tent for seven days while they are ordained (Leviticus 8:33-35), and a bull is offered each day (verse 36).

decisions.choice: fill their hand: ordain them
decisions.reason: See verse 9.

source.text: וּפַ֨ר חַטָּ֜את תַּעֲשֶׂ֤ה לַיּוֹם֙ עַל־הַכִּפֻּרִ֔ים וְחִטֵּאתָ֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ בְּכַפֶּרְךָ֖ עָלָ֑יו וּמָֽשַׁחְתָּ֥ אֹת֖וֹ לְקַדְּשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And a young bull of sin offering you will offer for the day for the atonement, and you will purify the altar when you make atonement on it, and anoint it to consecrate it.

en.L: And a bull of sin offering you shall offer each day for the atonement, and you shall purify the altar when you make atonement for it, and you shall anoint it to consecrate it.
en.B: Every day you are to offer a bull as a sin offering for atonement. You will cleanse the altar from sin as you make atonement for it, and you will anoint the altar so that it is consecrated.
en.R: Each day, offer a bull as a sin offering to make atonement. Make the altar pure by making atonement for it. Then anoint it with oil to make it holy.

decisions.choice: purify: cleanse from sin
alternatives: offer a sin offering on the altar
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the root for sin and here means to remove sin's defilement, to make clean (Leviticus 8:15; Psalm 51:9). It may also be read as "offer a sin offering on the altar".

decisions.choice: atonement for the altar: the altar itself must be cleansed
decisions.reason: The altar is made by human hands and stands among a sinful people, so it too must be cleansed and consecrated before it can be used (Leviticus 8:15; 16:18-19).

decisions.choice: each day for the atonement: one bull on each of the seven days
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean that the bull is for making atonement, or that it is offered in addition to the other offerings of atonement.

source.text: שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֗ים תְּכַפֵּר֙ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְקִדַּשְׁתָּ֖ אֹת֑וֹ וְהָיָ֤ה הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ קֹ֣דֶשׁ קָֽדָשִׁ֔ים כָּל־הַנֹּגֵ֥עַ בַּמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ יִקְדָּֽשׁ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Seven days you will make atonement on the altar and consecrate it, and will be the altar holiness of holinesses; all the [thing which] touches the altar will be holy.

en.L: Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and consecrate it, and the altar shall be most holy; whatever touches the altar shall become holy.
en.B: Seven days in a row you are to make atonement for the altar and consecrate it, and so it will become most holy. Anything that comes into contact with the altar will become holy.
en.R: Do this for seven days: make atonement for the altar and make it holy. Then the altar will be most holy. Anything that touches it will become holy too.

decisions.choice: holiness of holinesses: most holy, holy in the highest degree
decisions.reason: Doubling a noun in this way makes a superlative, as in "the holy of holies" (26:33). The altar is holy in the highest degree.

decisions.choice: whatever touches the altar will become holy
alternatives: whatever touches the altar must be holy
whoever touches the altar will become holy
decisions.reason: The verb can say what happens or what is required. It may mean that whatever touches the altar takes on its holiness and now belongs to God, or that only what is holy may touch it. The same phrase is used of the tabernacle's furnishings in 30:29; compare Haggai 2:12-13. The word "whatever" may also include persons.

source.text: וְזֶ֕ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כְּבָשִׂ֧ים בְּנֵֽי־שָׁנָ֛ה שְׁנַ֥יִם לַיּ֖וֹם תָּמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And this [is] what you will offer on the altar: lambs, sons of a year, two for the day, continually.

en.L: And this [is] what you shall offer on the altar: lambs, sons of a year, two each day, continually.
en.B: Here is what you will offer on the altar day by day, without fail: two lambs in their first year.
en.R: Every day, without ever missing a day, offer two lambs on the altar. They must be one year old.

decisions.choice: continually: regularly, every day without a break
decisions.reason: The word means constant or regular. The daily offering is never left off (verse 42; Numbers 28:3-8).

decisions.choice: sons of a year: a year old, in their first year
decisions.reason: As in 12:5.

source.text: אֶת־הַכֶּ֥בֶשׂ הָאֶחָ֖ד תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה בַבֹּ֑קֶר וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֥ין הָעַרְבָּֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: The lamb, the one, you will offer in the morning, and the lamb, the second, you will offer between the evenings.

en.L: The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer between the two evenings.
en.B: One lamb you are to offer in the morning, and the second as evening falls.
en.R: Offer one lamb in the morning and the other one as the sun goes down.

decisions.choice: between the two evenings: at twilight, as the day ends
decisions.reason: The same phrase sets the time of the Passover (12:6). Its exact meaning is uncertain: between sunset and dark, or from the sun's turning toward evening until sunset. See the note at 12:6.

decisions.choice: as evening falls / as the sun goes down
decisions.reason: As in 12:6. Literal keeps "between the two evenings".

source.text: וְעִשָּׂרֹ֨ן סֹ֜לֶת בָּל֨וּל בְּשֶׁ֤מֶן כָּתִית֙ רֶ֣בַע הַהִ֔ין וְנֵ֕סֶךְ רְבִעִ֥ית הַהִ֖ין יָ֑יִן לַכֶּ֖בֶשׂ הָאֶחָֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil, pressed, a fourth of the hin, and a drink offering, a fourth of the hin of wine, for the lamb, the one.

en.L: And a tenth [of an ephah] of fine flour mixed with a fourth of a hin of pressed oil, and a drink offering of a fourth of a hin of wine, for the one lamb.
en.B: Along with the one lamb, there is to be {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of fine flour mixed with {{units:about 1 quart|a quarter of a hin}} of pure pressed olive oil, and for a drink offering, {{units:about 1 quart|a quarter of a hin}} of wine.
en.R: With the first lamb, offer {{units:about 2 quarts|a tenth of an ephah}} of the best flour mixed with {{units:about 1 quart|a quarter of a hin}} of olive oil. Also pour out {{units:about 1 quart|a quarter of a hin}} of wine as a drink offering.

decisions.choice: a tenth: a tenth of an ephah of flour
decisions.reason: The ephah was a dry measure of about 20 quarts, or half a bushel, so a tenth of it was about 2 quarts (16:36). The measure was later called a tenth of an ephah in full (Numbers 28:5).

decisions.choice: a fourth of the hin: about 1 quart
decisions.reason: The hin was a liquid measure of about 1 gallon, so a quarter of it was about 1 quart.

decisions.choice: pressed oil: oil from crushed olives, the finest
decisions.reason: The oil was beaten or pressed from olives rather than squeezed out by heavy crushing, which gave the clearest oil, as for the lamp (27:20).

decisions.choice: about 2 quarts ... about 1 quart
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure first, with the original unit as the alternative. Literal keeps "a tenth" and "a fourth of a hin".

source.text: וְאֵת֙ הַכֶּ֣בֶשׂ הַשֵּׁנִ֔י תַּעֲשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ין הָעַרְבָּ֑יִם כְּמִנְחַ֨ת הַבֹּ֤קֶר וּכְנִסְכָּהּ֙ תַּֽעֲשֶׂה־לָּ֔הּ לְרֵ֣יחַ נִיחֹ֔חַ אִשֶּׁ֖ה לַיהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the lamb, the second, you will offer between the evenings; like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering you will offer with it, for an aroma of soothing, an offering by fire to Yahweh.

en.L: And the second lamb you shall offer between the two evenings; like the grain offering of the morning and like its drink offering you shall offer with it, for an aroma of soothing, an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The second lamb you will offer as evening falls. Prepare with it a grain offering and a drink offering like those of the morning, an offering by fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} whose aroma pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Offer the second lamb as the sun goes down. Offer the same grain offering and drink offering with it as you did in the morning. It is an offering burned with fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and its smell pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: grain offering: the flour and oil of verse 40
decisions.reason: The word means a gift or tribute. In the laws of offering it names the offering of flour, oil and grain (Leviticus 2).

decisions.choice: an aroma of soothing: an offering God accepts
decisions.reason: As in verse 18.

source.text: עֹלַ֤ת תָּמִיד֙ לְדֹרֹ֣תֵיכֶ֔ם פֶּ֥תַח אֹֽהֶל־מוֹעֵ֖ד לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר אִוָּעֵ֤ד לָכֶם֙ שָׁ֔מָּה לְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ שָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: A burnt offering of continuity for your generations [at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting before Yahweh, where I will meet to you there to speak to you there.

en.L: [It shall be] a continual burnt offering throughout your generations [at] the entrance of the tent of meeting before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, where I will meet with you, to speak to you there.
en.B: This is to be the regular burnt offering, generation after generation, at the doorway of the tent of meeting before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. That is where I will meet with you, to speak to you.
en.R: For all time to come, your people must offer this burnt offering every day. Offer it in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} at the door of the tent of meeting. That is where I will meet with you and talk with you.

decisions.choice: I will meet: come to meet at an appointed place
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet by appointment. It shares its root with "meeting" in "tent of meeting": the tent is the place where God meets with Moses and with Israel (25:22; 30:6, 36).

decisions.choice: you ... you: first the people, then Moses
decisions.reason: The first "you" is plural, meaning Israel, with whom God meets; the second is singular, meaning Moses, to whom God speaks. God meets with the people and speaks to Moses.

decisions.choice: your people must offer this burnt offering every day
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "continual" and "for your generations" as the people's lasting duty.

source.text: וְנֹעַדְתִּ֥י שָׁ֖מָּה לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְנִקְדַּ֖שׁ בִּכְבֹדִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will meet there with [the] sons of Israel, and it will be made holy by my glory.

en.L: And I will meet there with the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and it shall be made holy by {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory.
en.B: There I will meet with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory will make the tent holy.
en.R: I will meet with the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} there, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory will make the place holy.

decisions.choice: it will be made holy: the tent, the place where God meets Israel
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It most likely means the tent of meeting (verse 44), the place where God meets his people. It may also mean Israel, made holy by God's presence, or it may mean that God shows himself holy.

decisions.choice: my glory: God's visible presence
decisions.reason: The glory of Yahweh is his presence made visible, as on Sinai (24:16-17). When the tabernacle is finished, the cloud covers it and his glory fills it (40:34-35).

decisions.choice: the tent / the place
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is made holy, following the most likely reading.

source.text: וְקִדַּשְׁתִּ֛י אֶת־אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד וְאֶת־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְאֶת־אַהֲרֹ֧ן וְאֶת־בָּנָ֛יו אֲקַדֵּ֖שׁ לְכַהֵ֥ן לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar; and Aaron and his sons I will consecrate to serve as priests to me.

en.L: And I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar; and Aaron and his sons I will consecrate to serve as priests to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: The tent of meeting and the altar I will make holy, and Aaron and his sons I will set apart as holy to serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.
en.R: I will make the tent of meeting and the altar holy. I will also make Aaron and his sons holy so they can serve {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} as priests.

decisions.choice: I will consecrate: God himself makes them holy
decisions.reason: Moses carries out the rites (verses 1, 21, 36-37), but it is God who makes the tent, the altar and the priests holy. The verse repeats the purpose with which the chapter began (verse 1).

source.text: וְשָׁ֣כַנְתִּ֔י בְּת֖וֹךְ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָהֶ֖ם לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will dwell in [the] midst of [the] sons of Israel and I will be to them God.

en.L: And I will dwell in the midst of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, and I will be God to them.
en.B: I will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} home among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and I will be their God.
en.R: I will live among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, and I will be their God.

decisions.choice: I will dwell among them and be their God: the goal of the tabernacle and of the exodus
decisions.reason: These verses are the high point of the instructions for the tabernacle. The sanctuary was to be made so that God could dwell among his people (25:8), and here he promises to do so. They also fulfill the promise of 6:7, "I will take you as my people, and I will be your God", spoken before the exodus began. The promise is repeated in Leviticus 26:11-12 and is taken up in Revelation 21:3.

decisions.choice: dwell: settle and live, as in a tent
decisions.reason: The verb means to settle or to live in a place. The word for the tabernacle, "dwelling", comes from the same root (25:8-9).

source.text: וְיָדְע֗וּ כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹצֵ֧אתִי אֹתָ֛ם מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לְשָׁכְנִ֣י בְתוֹכָ֑ם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they will know that I [am] Yahweh their God, who brought them out from [the] land of Egypt, to dwell I among them; I [am] Yahweh their God.

en.L: And they shall know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God, who brought them out from the land of Egypt that I might dwell in their midst; I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.
en.B: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. I brought them out of the land of Egypt for this purpose, to make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} home among them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.
en.R: Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God. I brought them out of Egypt so that I could live among them. I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} their God.

decisions.choice: brought them out ... to dwell among them: the purpose of the exodus
decisions.reason: God did not bring Israel out of Egypt only to free them from slavery, but so that he might live among them. The exodus and the tabernacle belong together.

decisions.choice: to dwell: a purpose clause
alternatives: they will know ... when I dwell among them
decisions.reason: The form most likely states the purpose of bringing them out. It may also be read as stating when they will know it: when God dwells among them.

decisions.choice: they will know that I am Yahweh: the refrain of the exodus
decisions.reason: The words "you will know that I am Yahweh" run through the exodus story (6:7; 7:5; 14:4, 18). Now Israel will know it, not from God's judgments on Egypt but from his presence among them.
